problem: POST /stock-transfers is on the through-HO submit list, but stock_transfer is approved by the company's MANAGERS, is non-delegable, and is exempt from the through-HO rule (§7.4.1). An HOD's stock-transfer request therefore never reaches the CEO, which breaks D3 ('initially HODs submit approval to me'), and it can never be handed to the HOD either.
change: Remove `POST /stock-transfers` from HO_SUBMIT_ROUTES in v1. A reach-only caller gets 403 HEAD_OFFICE_SUBMIT_ONLY. Alternative: when `submittedThroughHeadOffice` is true, make stock_transfer CEO-routed and delegable under 'procurement'. Add a test that a lens POST /stock-transfers returns 403.

problem: resolveTenantScope reads the `x-servd-portfolio` header whatever the HTTP method (backend/src/lib/tenantScope.ts L40-62). Today only the middleware's tenantFilter is GET-gated. Under the spec, portfolio = member ∪ reach, so a non-GET request that carries `x-servd-portfolio: 1` (forged, or from any client) puts reached companies into every write route that does lookups in 'read' mode (e.g. recipes L620, scopeTenantWhere(req,'read')). That is direct write reach without the submit allow-list.
change: In resolveTenantScope, add reachTenantIds only when req.method is GET/HEAD. For non-GET, portfolio = memberTenantIds ∪ [submitTenantId], the same as tenantFilter. Add a headOfficeReach.test case: a POST with x-servd-portfolio:1 from a reach-only user cannot resolve a reached company's row through any 'read'-mode lookup.

problem: 'Through head office' requires the submitter NOT to be a member of the item's company. Today's HODs (Procurement, Finance, Marketing in GS Foods) are TenantMembers of GS Foods and the JV, and they stay members until the CA's cutover month K, or longer for anyone the CEO ticks 'keep'. Until then every HOD submission goes to company approvers, and their writes stay direct. D3 ('separate approvals for all HODs … submit to me') is not delivered until K. The rule is also evaluated against the CURRENT link: if a link is ended after submission, the item drops out of the CEO route.
change: Redefine it as: through HO = some submitter is a non-admin member of a head office whose link to the item's company was live at the item's submit time (link.startedAt ≤ submittedAt < coalesce(endedAt, ∞)). Being a member of the company does NOT exempt them. In the setup wizard (§14.3), add an optional CEO-ticked step: 'add these HOD logins as members of GS Head Office now' (TenantMember only; payroll still moves at K). Document that direct writes by dual members remain possible until their company membership is removed, and show this on the People tab. Add tests: a dual-member HOD's PO/recipe/payroll lands in the CEO inbox and a company GM gets 403; ending the link after submission keeps the item with the CEO.

problem: (a) §4.6 and the test say 'a company-scoped Finance delegate approves' an ic_transfer, but §7.4.2 requires the delegation to cover EVERY tenant in touchesTenantIds, which is [HO, company]. A company-scoped grant never covers the HO, so the rule and the test contradict each other. (b) The 409 SECTION_HANDED_TO_OTHER_HEAD_OFFICE rule means that when C sits under H1 and H2 and H1 holds an HO-wide Finance grant, H2 can never get an HO-wide Finance grant. ho_recharge requires an HO-wide grant, so H2's own recharge runs (and its transfers with C) stay CEO-only for ever, although they are unambiguously H2's items.
change: Split coverage by who owns the item. HO-owned types (ho_recharge, ic_transfer) are covered when delegation.tenantId === item.tenantId (the owning HO) and, for ic_transfer, the grant is HO-wide or companyTenantId === item.companyTenantId. These types are exempt from the one-HO-per-(company, section) check. Company-owned types (purchase_order, recipe, hr_request, payroll_run, tip_pool, journal_request, connector_change, staff_login, storefront_publish) keep the 'covers every touched tenant' rule and the uniqueness check, and the uniqueness check runs over company-owned types only. Fix the §12 tests to match: a company-scoped H-Finance delegate approves an H↔C transfer, and H2 can hold an HO-wide Finance grant for its own runs while H1 holds C's company-owned Finance types.

problem: 'Load the row by id with no scope' still goes through the RLS-extended `prisma` client. In production (RLS_ENFORCE=1) the delegate's context holds only its own memberships until assertCanApprove widens it, so the lookup that computes the company returns nothing and every delegated approve is a 404. Existing guards do the same today: guardPo uses supplierScopeWhere(req,'write'), and payroll approve/lock/reopen use writeTenants(req) (hr/routes.ts L1495-1530). Company members reading the run basis, split shares and the HO's due-from balance (§4.8) also hit tenant-only policies on recharge_runs, recharge_splits/lines, accounts and journal_lines of the HO tenant. Tests cannot see any of this because the test DB has no policies.
change: Specify a resolver per type: `approvalSubject(type, id)` runs on serviceClient, selects only {companyIds, submitterIds, status}, and runs BEFORE assertCanApprove. The module's handler then re-reads the row through `prisma` after widenRls. Replace guardPo / writeTenants / inTenants lookups on every rewired approve and queue route accordingly. Company-side intercompany reads (statement, reconciliation, run basis, current shares) run on serviceClient with explicit `companyTenantId ∈ member` filtering. Alternatively, add RLS policies on recharge_runs, recharge_splits and recharge_split_lines that admit a company through an EXISTS on its line or link; pick one and write it in §2.2. Keep the manual RLS check, and extend it to one delegated payroll lock and one company-side statement read.

problem: Several allow-listed routes let a reach-only HOD change or destroy company-owned work directly, with no approval. (1) `DELETE /hr/payroll/runs/:id` is allowed on ANY draft run, including one prepared by company HR. (2) `POST /hr/payroll/runs` can pre-empt the company's own run for the period (@@unique([tenantId, period]) → the company's HR gets 409 EXISTS). (3) `PUT /recipes/:id` and `POST /recipes/:id/test-attempts` are allowed on ANY recipe in iteration. Recipe has no createdById or editor list, so if the company chef later submits, a company owner approves the HOD's edits and the CEO route is bypassed. (4) `POST /hr/records/offer/:id/create-employee` is allowed on ANY approved offer.
change: (1) DELETE only when run.createdById === caller and run.preparedByIds ⊆ {caller}. (2) POST /hr/payroll/runs through the lens is allowed only when no run exists for the period (as today), and is audited with viaHeadOfficeId. (3) Add `createdById String?` and `editedByIds String[] @default([])` to Recipe in the same migration. PUT, test-attempts and submit append the caller. Through the lens, PUT and test-attempts are allowed only on recipes with createdById === caller. submittedByIds for recipe approval = createdById ∪ editedByIds ∪ submittedById, so any HO editor routes the recipe to the CEO. (4) create-employee through the lens only for offers with createdById === caller.

area: §7.4.3 separation of duties for the new pending records
problem: Self-approval protection relies on submittedByIds, but the new records do not track editors. IntercompanyTransfer has `PATCH /intercompany/transfers/:id` with no stated editor rule. RechargeRun `refresh` is open to any HO preparer. PosConnectorChange/JournalRequest only record preparedById. A Finance delegate who edits another preparer's transfer amount, or refreshes a run, and then approves it, passes the 'not preparer/submitter' check.
change: Add `preparedByIds String[] @default([])` to JournalRequest, RechargeRun, IntercompanyTransfer and PosConnectorChange, following HrPayrollRun.preparedByIds. Every create, PATCH, refresh and submit appends the actor inside the same claim (updateMany where status in editable). submittedByIds = preparedByIds ∪ {preparedById, submittedById}. The approve claim adds `NOT: { preparedByIds: { has: me } }` for non-admins, the same as hr/routes.ts L1507. PATCH of a transfer or journal request is allowed only to the original preparer, or the change must be tracked as above. Add tests: an editor-then-approver gets 403 SELF_APPROVAL_BLOCKED for each of the four.

problem: A true-up stores priorCents and baseCents at preparation. If the CEO reverses the month's monthly run while the true-up is submitted, approving the true-up posts a base computed against a prior that no longer exists. The month is then mis-recharged until a further true-up. The approval-time recompute only records the drift and does not refuse.
change: At approve, inside the advisory lock, recompute prior. If it differs from run.priorCents → 409 RUN_STALE ('refresh the run'). CEO reverse of any run withdraws every open (draft/submitted) run for the same (HO, period) in the same transaction, audited ho.recharge.withdraw with reason 'superseded by reversal'. True-ups use the split of the first POSTED, NON-REVERSED run.

problem: Recharge postings are excluded from the pool only by reference prefix and excludeCodes ['6990']. If nextFreeCode picks 6991-6999, or the CA re-maps the recharge account to another expense code, the account is not in excludeCodes. Any non-recharge line on it (an IC transfer that uses it as hoCounter, or a manual JE) then feeds back into the pool.
change: computePool always excludes HeadOfficeBooks.rechargeAccountId, whatever the codes in costPool. validateMapping and the transfer route refuse the recharge account, and every link's due accounts, as a transfer counter (422 COUNTER_ACCOUNT_INVALID). The manual-journal path refuses the recharge account too: treat it as controlledBy='head_office' or add a separate 'recharge' marker that postJournalEntry checks the same way.

problem: One common open date for ALL books means that one locked company pushes every other company's charge for month M into a later month, even when their own books (and the HO's) are open for M. This distorts monthly P&Ls that did not need to move.
change: Compute the date per pair: date(line) = max(default M-end date, day after max(lockedThrough(HO), lockedThrough(company))). Both entries of a line share that date, so invariant 1 (per pair, per date) still holds. The run stores per-line entryDate and postedLate. Keep the one-transaction, all-or-nothing posting.

problem: Ending a link auto-creates a split version effective lastChargedPeriod+1. That collides with the SPLIT_PERIOD_IN_USE rule when submitted or posted runs exist for later periods, and the spec says nothing about which rule wins. lastChargedPeriod is also not validated against runs already posted for the company.
change: Validate lastChargedPeriod ≥ the latest period with a submitted, posted or draft run line for that company (422 RUN_AFTER_LAST_CHARGED, listing them). The auto version goes through the same SPLIT_PERIOD_IN_USE check (409 with 'withdraw or reverse those runs first'). Draft runs after lastChargedPeriod are marked stale.

area: §7.5 delegation life cycle vs link changes
problem: A company-scoped delegation is suspended by unlinking but silently revives if the CEO re-links the company later, because re-linking clears endedAt on the same row and the live check passes again. An HO-wide grant also silently extends to every company linked later, which the CEO may not expect.
change: Ending a link revokes, in the same transaction, every unrevoked delegation with companyTenantId = that company and tenantId = that HO (revokeReason 'company unlinked', audited). The link dialog lists the HO-wide delegations that will cover the new company and requires the CEO to tick 'extend these hand-overs' or revoke them. Add both cases to approvalDelegation.test.ts.

area: §7.4/§7.5 company under two head offices: who approves
problem: Items in C submitted by an H2 HOD go to H1's delegate whenever (C, section) is handed to H1. One head office's HOD then approves another head office's submissions, which is not what 'assign the approval right of their section to them' means.
change: Delegation coverage of a through-HO item also requires the submitter's head office (the one the through-HO check matched) to equal delegation.tenantId. Otherwise the item stays with the CEO. Items submitted by the company's own staff use the (company, section) holder as specified. Add to headOfficeTwoHeadOffices.test.ts.

problem: The new guard blocks any non-admin approver whose own payslip is on the run. Company management roles are normally on their company's payroll, so every existing company payroll silently becomes CEO-only on deploy. Neither the owner nor D3 asked for this.
change: In v1, apply OWN_PAY_IN_RUN to the delegation path and to runs of head-office tenants only. Raise it as an owner question for company role approvers, and switch it on there only after a yes. Adjust the hrHeadOffice tests.

problem: The old pieces are retired at deploy, before the setup wizard has moved what they feed. (1) 'server sets share = gross on any change to monthlySalaryCents' silently changes planning for a not-yet-normalised shared seat when someone edits its salary before the wizard runs, which is exactly the silent number change the spec says it avoids. (2) PATCH of an existing head_office contribution is refused (USE_HEAD_OFFICE) before any head office exists, so its amount cannot be corrected in the gap.
change: Until the setup marker exists: keep share unchanged on salary edits by scaling it by new/old salary, and allow PATCH of existing head_office rows (only POST of new ones is refused). After the marker: as specified. Add both to labourBudgetHeadOffice.test.ts.

problem: The standing duplicates rule is not applied to HR: forms.ts already has a 'transfer' HR record section (Movement, specNo 21, [HOD, HR]) whose effect changes branch, department and manager. The new hr/transfer.ts cross-company move overlaps it in name and purpose. Carried leave (and any gratuity or encashment accrued for past service, with 'keep joining date') also moves a liability to the HO with no intercompany entry.
change: Add a row to the §1 table for the HR 'transfer' section with the decision: keep both. The section is within one company; the new tool is CEO-only and crosses companies, and the section's newManager/newDepartment must refuse ids from another company. Label the new tool 'Move to head office'. In §0 and §14 add a CA question: whether carried leave balances and service-linked liabilities are settled by an IntercompanyTransfer adjustment (company → HO) at transfer. The preview shows the carried leave days × daily rate as a suggested amount.

problem: Only controlled (due-to/due-from) accounts are protected from deactivation. Deactivating the HO's recharge account or a company's 'Head office charges — H' account makes every later approve fail with ACCOUNT_NOT_FOUND (500), and breaks the CEO reversal of earlier runs, because reverseJournalEntry resolves codes against active accounts only.
change: PATCH /setup/chart-of-accounts/:id refuses isActive:false on any account referenced by HeadOfficeBooks.rechargeAccountId or HeadOfficeLink.chargesAccountId, with 422 ACCOUNT_MAPPED_TO_HEAD_OFFICE ('re-map it on the head office Books tab first').

problem: Reached companies are added to /tenants/mine, but TenantPicker.tsx, PortfolioWriteGuardModal.tsx and hooks/useEnsureTenant.ts (all consumers of that list for write pickers) are in no stream. They would offer reached companies for ordinary writes, which then fail with 403 HEAD_OFFICE_SUBMIT_ONLY.
change: Return reach in a separate field (`/tenants/mine` → `{ companies: [...members], reach: [...] }` or keep the array and add a top-level `reach`), so existing consumers are unchanged. Add those three files to Stream D, with a filter that keeps reach out of every write picker.

problem: Once a non-member delegate can run approve handlers, any side effect that reads req.staffUser.tenantId, activeTenant(req) or scopeTenantWhere(req,'create') (audit tenantId, activity rows, exceptions, notifications, default config rows) lands in the delegate's head office instead of the item's company.
change: Rule for every rewired route (PO, recipe, staff login, storefront, payroll approve/lock/reopen, tip pool post/pay, HR decide, journal request, connector change, runs, transfers): every write after assertCanApprove takes the company from the item. Add one test per type: a delegated approval creates no row with tenantId = the HO, and the audit row carries the item's company.

problem: A reach-only HO HR user may decide a non-final 'hr' step directly. A REJECT at that step ends the company employee's request (leave, overtime, …) without the CEO or any delegation, which contradicts 'HOD actions are submitted for approval'.
change: Reach-only callers may APPROVE a non-final hr step (forward it). A reject at any step needs the role path for members or a live HR delegation covering rec.tenantId; otherwise 403 FINAL_STEP_NEEDS_HANDOVER. Add to hrHeadOffice.test.ts.

problem: Recipe has no tenantId. Its company is derived from the menu item's concept, pendingMenuItem or ingredients (recipes/routes.ts L142-230), and a component recipe can span several companies or none. ApprovalCheck.tenantId and touchesTenantIds are not defined for recipes, so delegation coverage, the through-HO check and lens creates are ambiguous.
change: Define it: recipe touchesTenantIds = the derived company set. An empty set means CEO-only (tenantId null). A lens `POST /recipes` must bind to the lens company: either pendingMenuItem.conceptId is a lens-company brand, or every ingredient's inventoryItem.tenantId is the lens company (422 otherwise). Delegation must cover every derived company.

problem: Posting manual journals is CEO-only today (POST /accounting/journal is ADMIN_ONLY). The brief's list of what can be handed over (POs, recipes, website, HR final sign-off, payroll, tip pools, bank adjustments, floor logins) does not include manual journals, yet the spec makes them delegable to Finance HODs without asking the owner.
change: Treat journal_request (kind post) like Marketing: a grant returns 422 SECTION_NOT_YET_DELEGABLE for that type until a constant is flipped after the owner confirms. Add it to the owner-question list.

problem: sectionOfModule(inventory) gives 'procurement', because approvalSection is set on the whole 'Stock & buying' section, which holds inventory, par_sheet and procurement. The rights table puts stock_transfer (queue module inventory) under 'operations'. There are two derivations and they disagree.
change: Make the section explicit per approval type in APPROVAL_RIGHTS, the single source, and test it against WORKSPACES only for workspace-level sections. Alternatively, drop approvalSection on the workspace section and map procurement → 'procurement' by module id. Also derive roleListAllows from APPROVAL_RIGHTS[type].roles and delete the module-local role constants for approve routes, so there is one copy of each approver list.

area: §6.7 head-office tenants in existing per-company code
problem: Many loops and pickers treat every Tenant as a trading company: the riders FleetAgreement tenant picker (riders/routes.ts L115), POS connector rows and fiscal /health (a head office would default to 'fiscal reporting required' with no live connector), scheduled reports, CRM segments and loyalty workers. Only primaryTenantId and location seeding are filtered.
change: Add a sweep task to Stream A or B. FleetAgreement create refuses kind head_office (422). ensureConnectorRow and fiscal /health skip head offices. Workers that compute sales, CRM or loyalty filter kind:'company'. List each file in its stream.

problem: (1) seed-positions.ts (Stream C) and the setup wizard need Stream A's create, link and split functions, which are not among A's exports. (2) lib/separation-of-duties.ts (assertNotSelfApproval, used by B) is owned by no stream. (3) Minor text errors: the spec refers to '§8.3' (it means §7.3), says 'nine tables' (there are ten), and says reversal sourceType 'ho.recharge.reversal:<lineId>' where reverseJournalEntry stores reference `${sourceType}.reversal:${sourceId}`. The pool's 'ho.recharge%' prefix does match it.
change: Add `createHeadOffice(tx, …)`, `linkCompany(tx, …)`, `createSplitVersion(tx, …)` to A's hour-0 exports. Assign lib/separation-of-duties.ts to Stream B. Fix the references: §7.3, ten tables. State that reversal entries are stored as `ho.recharge.reversal:<lineId>` / `ho.transfer.reversal:<id>`, and that the pool excludes by `reference LIKE 'ho.recharge%'` (which covers both).
